text:
sam: FYI we have a Solara Health POC kickoff tomorrow 10am PT. They want Redwood Private deployed into their VPCs. Can we confirm recommended connectivity patterns (peering vs PrivateLink vs central proxy), how we handle egress IP stability, and a minimal firewall allowlist to hand to their security team?

iris: High level options: 1) VPC peering (straight path, preserves client src IP), 2) AWS PrivateLink/interface endpoints (isolated, no route changes, IAM principal controls), 3) Shared-services proxy (centralized NAT/NLB or reverse proxy in a hub VPC). Each has tradeoffs around client IP preservation, egress SNAT, auditability, and operational approvals.

devon: If they require original source IP in app logs for audit/compliance -> VPC peering or an L3-transparent router appliance. PrivateLink by default will terminate at ENIs and source will be our endpoint; shared-proxy will SNAT unless configured with proxy-pass headers and app-level correlation.

alice: Security notes from their SRE: they run TLS inspection on egress and need 12 months of firewall logs. They also have SD-WAN sites with MTU ~1400. Any special network config we should call out?

iris: MTU/fragmentation: SD-WAN + tunneling reduces path MTU. Recommend TCP MSS clamp on their routers or enforce MSS ~1360 on tunnels. If using NAT gateways or proxies, extra headers may push packets over MTU and cause fragmentation. PrivateLink ENIs do not change MTU by themselves but can still hit fragmentation if downstream VPN overlays exist.

devon: TLS inspection: if customer terminates and re-encrypts (re-sign) traffic to us, fine. If they do inline interception, they must allow SNI passthrough for our certs to validate, or else cert pinning will fail. For auditables, VPC peering is simplest to preserve src IP.

sam: Procurement asked: cost comparison PrivateLink vs Peering for data egress. Any rough guidance?

devon: Rough guidance (AWS): PrivateLink = endpoint-hour + per-GB processed on interface endpoints + data transfer to endpoint. VPC peering = cross-AZ/data transfer charges. For sustained high-volume egress, peering often wins on raw $/GB; PrivateLink is simpler for cross-account access and reduces routing/approval blast radius. I can run a cost delta if you provide expected GB/month and AZ count.

iris: Ops overhead: peering requires route table changes, potential security approvals for cross-account peering. PrivateLink avoids route changes but needs ENI placement in subnets and IAM/principal policies. Shared proxy centralizes egress (good for audit/inspection) but adds ops on that proxy (scaling, healthchecks) and you need stable EIPs.

devon: Minimal firewall allowlist (send to their firewall team):

```text
# Example minimal outbound allowlist for Redwood Private
ALLOW tcp 443 to 203.0.113.45/32   # replace with assigned NLB EIP(s) or proxy EIPs
ALLOW tcp 443 to 198.51.100.12/32
# If using PrivateLink -> allow to interface endpoint ENI IPs in customer's subnets (no route changes)
# ICMP/UDP not required unless you run custom transports
```

iris: Route table example for peering:

```text
# Customer route table
Destination: 10.60.0.0/16 -> pcx-0abc123def4567890
# Ensure security groups/NACLs allow the relevant CIDRs between VPCs
```

netops-bot: Attached SG template + quick runbook -> https://internal.redwood/sales/configs/privatedeploy-netops-sg.json

alice: Compliance asks: they need 12-month retention for firewall logs and proof of chain-of-custody for any exported logs. We should confirm log formats (CEF/JSON) and whether we provide sampling or full-burst capture.

sam: Action items before the call: devon -> cost delta table (peering vs privatelink vs shared-proxy) given GB estimate; iris -> one-page netops checklist including MSS clamp snippets and SG/ACL template; sam -> invite customer neteng + legal on retention; alice -> collect their VPC CIDRs, AZ count, and expected GB/month.

devon: I'll DM procurement for the GB estimate and produce a simple spreadsheet with $/GB assumptions by region and AZ count. ETA: EOD PT today.

iris: I'll prepare MSS clamp commands (Cisco/Juniper/iptables examples) and a minimal SG template for the call. Will upload to the thread. ✅

alice: I'll upload their initial network diagram and security questionnaire answers by 8am PT tomorrow so we can iterate on the runbook before the 10am call.

sam: Good. If anyone has a short Q/A snippet to pre-send to the customer neteng (to speed approvals), drop it in here and I'll include in the invite.

devon: Pre-ask snippet suggestion: 1) Provide VPC CIDR(s) and peering/endpoint subnets, 2) Confirm list of AZs and whether cross-AZ traffic is billed in your account, 3) Provide expected monthly egress (GB) and typical concurrent connections, 4) Confirm whether TLS inspection will be inline or re-encrypting.

iris: Also ask if they require client IP preservation in application logs or if x-forwarded-for style headers are acceptable.

sam: Perfect — thanks team. See you on the call tomorrow.
